text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Credit Agricole posts a 7.5 billion franc profit for 1996, seeks to develop international activities and considers entering consumer-credit market.
-- European stock exchanges ignore U.S. Federal Reserve Board's decision to raise rates, remain optimistic.

-- A planned merger between Lyonnaise des Eaux and Suez may take the form of a takeover of Suez by Lyonnaise des Eaux without a share exchange. A deal would be submitted to the companies' board meetings next week.
-- Bank of France expected to leave rates unchanged at this morning's monetary policy council.
-- Generale des Eaux weighs sale of cable-TV activity to Time Warner.
-- Dassault seen taking less than 25 percent of Aerospatiale, chairman Serge Dassault to negotiate with the government in April.

-- Bank of France Monetary Policy Council member Jean-Pierre Gerard does not rule out a delay in the implementation of a single European currency, adds Bank of France has room to cut repo rate by 10 basis points.
-- Disneyland Paris theme park expects some 12 million visitors in 1997.
-- Finance Ministry seeks to maintain revenues from taxes on tobacco, while industrialists call for price cuts to fend off lag in consumption.
-- Legal authorities block sale of part of Chateau Yquem to LVMH on technical grounds at the request of one of the owners who is trying to prevent the sale.
-- Axa profit jumps 40 percent for 1996 from 1995 while UAP absorbs charges and posts a 6.45 billion franc loss.
